name: Atelectasis
description: Volume loss and collapse of alveolar units seen as linear or wedge-shaped opacities with fissure displacement.
clinical_significance: Frequently seen post-operatively, secondary to hypoventilation, mucus plugging, or airway obstruction.

name: Cardiomegaly
description: Enlargement of the cardiac silhouette exceeding 50% of the maximum thoracic diameter on PA projection.
clinical_significance: Associated with heart failure, cardiomyopathy, pericardial effusion, or valvular disease.

name: Consolidation
description: Homogeneous opacification obscuring pulmonary vascular margins, typically with patent air-filled bronchi.
clinical_significance: Indicates replacement of alveolar air with fluid, blood, pus, or neoplastic cells.

name: Infiltration
description: Abnormal opacification representing fluid, cellular exudate, or fibrosis within the lung parenchyma.
clinical_significance: Broad differential diagnosis including non-specific inflammatory, edema, or atypical infectious processes.

name: Mass
description: Circumscribed pulmonary or mediastinal lesion greater than 3 cm in diameter.
clinical_significance: Radiographic morphologic finding, not confirmed malignancy. Benign etiologies (granulomas, hamartomas, organizing pneumonia) present identically; tissue biopsy and CT are required for definitive histological diagnosis.

name: Nodule
description: Discrete rounded opacity less than 3 cm in diameter surrounded by aerated lung parenchyma.
clinical_significance: Solitary or multiple pulmonary nodules warranting Fleischner Society surveillance criteria. A low score does not rule out lung cancer, and a high score does not confirm malignancy.

name: Pneumonia
description: Inflammatory consolidation or alveolar infiltrates within pulmonary airspace, often with air bronchograms.
clinical_significance: Acute infectious etiology requiring clinical correlation with vitals, auscultation, and biomarkers.

name: Pneumothorax
description: Presence of gas within the pleural cavity with a visible visceral pleural line and absent peripheral lung markings.
clinical_significance: Critical acute finding; tension physiology mandates immediate clinical decompression.

name: Pleural Effusion
description: Blunting of the lateral or posterior costophrenic sulci due to fluid accumulation in the pleural cavity.
clinical_significance: Indicative of transudative or exudative fluid collections (e.g., CHF, infection, malignancy).

name: No Finding
description: Clear lung fields, normal cardiothoracic ratio, sharp costophrenic angles, and intact bony thorax.
clinical_significance: Does not constitute proof of a normal radiograph or absence of cancer. Early malignancies, sub-centimeter nodules, central endobronchial lesions, or non-targeted pathologies cannot be excluded on radiograph alone.
